chunks: (Moses) said: "Go hence! All your life you are (cursed) to say: 'Do not touch me; and a threat hangs over you which you will not be able to escape. Look at your god to whom you are so attached: We shall verily burn it, and disperse its ashes into the sea."

key_terms.لاَ مِسَاسَ: Do not touch (a curse of exile)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'La Masas' and the fate of Pharaoh's idol mentioned in Surah Taa-Haa?
ai.summary: In this verse, Allah commands Pharaoh to depart, granting him a reprieve from immediate death but imposing the curse of 'La Masas' (no touching of the body after death) as a sign of his impurity. The promise of a specific, unchangeable appointment ('maw'idan') refers to his eventual death, while the destruction of his idol by fire and scattering its ashes into the sea symbolizes the complete nullification of his false divinity. This narrative underscores the transient nature of earthly power compared to divine decree.
